title: Square-root PSD area reduced row prediction error for 155 stored ferret spine simulations
abstract: We tested two size-to-voltage mappings in a public export for 155 spines from five ferret visual cortex cells. The voltage values are stored simulation outputs, not measured somatic responses. We compared linear area and square-root area models with an intercept in 100 repeated five-fold row splits. The square-root model reduced root mean squared error from 0.1923 to 0.1496 mV, or 22.2%. It had lower error in every split and after the largest 10% of areas were removed. Added neck length and its interaction with square-root area gave 0.1530 mV error. The associated example code sets AMPA conductance in proportion to square-root area. The result is thus a useful check of a simulation surrogate, not new evidence for a biological scaling law. Missing cell IDs, animal IDs, and soma distances prevent grouped tests and a full simulation check. We supply source hashes, retrieval code, predictions, numerical checks, and a figure.

display.caption: Stored simulated somatic responses and row prediction errors. Each model is trained without its test rows. The lines in panel A use all rows for display only. Panel B gives error over 100 five-fold splits. Panel C gives the mean error for each row. These outputs are from an existing simulation.
